author: stephtea
title: feat(robocall): self-serve resend for a payment-failed robocall
body:
## Why

A robocall's payment is a Stripe authorization hold. When the hold fails — most often on the deferred path, where the hold is placed off-session days after the candidate scheduled — the send silently dies: the row either hides from history (spine `pending_payment`) or shows as a normal "scheduled" row, and **there is no way for the candidate to re-enter payment.** The only intended recovery was a "update your card" email emitted as a fire-and-forget Segment milestone with no in-product fallback, so if that email doesn't deliver, the candidate is stranded with no self-serve path — exactly what happened to a real candidate whose Oct-17 robocall never went out and who had no way to fix it.

This adds the in-product recovery: a payment-failed robocall shows in history as **"Payment failed"**, and the candidate can update their card and resend — re-picking a future date, reusing the recording and script they already approved. No dependence on an email landing.

## What

**One money path, not a new one.** The resend reuses the exact draft-resume machinery. `OutreachService.findByScope` surfaces a robocall whose satellite `settleState === 'hold_failed'` (even at `pending_payment` spine) and exposes a minimal `robocall` block on the list row (`settleState`, `audioKey`, `callbackNumber`, `billableCount`) — mirroring the detail schema, no billing-column leak. `OutreachRobocallService.convertDraft` now accepts a `hold_failed` row alongside a `draft`: it re-runs the create gates (compliance/ETag bind, schedule validation on the **new** future date, server-re-derived billing) and lands the row back on `pending_payment`, where the existing authorize (`POST /outreach/robocall/:id/authorize`, which already accepts `hold_failed`) places the hold.

**Concurrency is interlocked, not just additive.** The single-winner claim moves onto the satellite settle-state CAS (`draft|hold_failed → pending_payment`). That serializes two concurrent resends *and* interlocks with the cancel-at-deadline sweep's `hold_failed → cancelled` CAS — exactly one of a resend and a mid-flight cancel can win, so a resend can never land on a row the sweep just cancelled, and a resumed row (now future-dated, off `hold_failed`) is no longer a sweep candidate.

**Frontend:** the row reads "Payment failed" (destructive badge); the drawer explains it and offers "Update card and resend," which re-enters `RobocallFlow` as a resume at the schedule step — recording, script, caller-ID and audience pre-seeded, the past date dropped so Continue stays disabled until a new future date is picked — then the pay step (unchanged; its existing `hold_failed` retry card still handles a repeat decline).

**Money safety unchanged:** billing is always re-derived server-side from the audience, never trusted from the client; promo codes a declined hold still carried (never redeemed) are re-read and re-priced against the fresh estimate.

## Note

This is the self-serve re-entry the robocall-payment doc had deferred as "a separate later slice." It does not replace the reliability work still worth doing (verifying the downstream HoldFailed/Reminder/Canceled email automation is wired, and a staff Slack alert on deferred-hold failure) — but it removes the single point of failure: the candidate now has an in-product way back regardless of whether any email lands.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches robocall draft conversion, outreach list filtering, and payment/settle-state CAS alongside the existing hold-failure cancel sweep; well covered by tests but errors could affect billing or history visibility.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **self-serve recovery** when a robocall’s pay-time Stripe hold fails: those sends stay visible in outreach history as **“Payment failed”** instead of being hidden like other `pending_payment` rows.
> 
> **API:** `findByScope` returns `hold_failed` robocalls with a minimal `robocall` block (`settleState`, `audioKey`, `callbackNumber`, `billableCount`). `convertDraft` on `POST /outreach/robocall` now resumes **`draft` or `hold_failed`** in place—schedule gates and billing re-derived server-side, with a **satellite settle-state CAS** (`draft|hold_failed → pending_payment`) so concurrent resends and the cancel-at-deadline sweep can’t both win.
> 
> **UI:** History and the details drawer show the failed-payment state; **“Update card and resend”** uses the same draft-resume path into `RobocallFlow` (new future date required; recording, script, and audience reused), then the existing authorize step. Product-knowledge copy documents the flow for assistants.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 52fb25fc9c4782ba6690ded20915d627fc6b4432. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
